descriptionChirho: To capture or seize a city, territory, or person by military force or decisive action (Qal active stem).
To catch or trap an animal or person by snare, net, or hunting, implying entrapment rather than military conquest (Qal active stem).
To be captured or taken, typically of a city or person falling to an enemy (Nifal passive stem).
To be caught or ensnared, as in a trap or snare, often used figuratively of being caught in wrongdoing (Nifal passive stem).
To freeze or become hard, said of water surfaces that solidify (Hitpael reflexive stem).
To cling together or hold fast to one another, describing things that are tightly interlocked (Hitpael reflexive stem).
